\section[\texorpdfstring{\ar{للمرة} \ar{الأولى} (li-l-marra al-ūlā)}{للمرة الأولى (li-l-marra al-ūlā)}]{\ar{للمرة} \ar{الأولى} (li-l-marra al-ūlā) — for the first time}

\label{lesson:AR-C349-li-l-marra-al-ula}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Arabic for to punish, then the Arabic for to inform the police.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ar{للمرة} \ar{الأولى}}
\textbf{\ar{للمرة} \ar{الأولى}} — \emph{li-l-marra al-ūlā} — \textquotedblleft{}for the first time\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ar{رأيت} \ar{البحر} \ar{للمرة} \ar{الأولى} \ar{في} \ar{حياتي}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{raʾaytu al-baḥr li-l-marra al-ūlā fī ḥayātī.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
I saw the sea for the first time in my life.
\end{quote}

Also \ar{لأول} \ar{مرة}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ar{للمرة} \ar{الأولى}} (\emph{li-l-marra al-ūlā}) is \textquotedblleft{}for the first passing\textquotedblright{}: \emph{marra} is built on the native Arabic root \emph{m-r-r}, \textquotedblleft{}to pass\textquotedblright{} (Lane), and \emph{ūlā} is the feminine of \emph{awwal}, first.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling what happened.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{li-l-marra al-ūlā}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{li-l-marra al-ūlā}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{raʾaytu al-baḥr li-l-marra al-ūlā fī ḥayātī.} — I saw the sea for the first time in my life.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Arabic for to punish, then the Arabic for to inform the police, then say \emph{li-l-marra al-ūlā} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \ar{للمرة} \ar{الأولى} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}For the first time\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[\texorpdfstring{\ar{عن} \ar{طريق} \ar{الخطأ} (ʿan ṭarīq al-khaṭaʾ)}{عن طريق الخطأ (ʿan ṭarīq al-khaṭaʾ)}]{\ar{عن} \ar{طريق} \ar{الخطأ} (ʿan ṭarīq al-khaṭaʾ) — by mistake}

\label{lesson:AR-C349-an-tariq-al-khata}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Arabic for to inform the police, then the Arabic for for the first time.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ar{عن} \ar{طريق} \ar{الخطأ}}
\textbf{\ar{عن} \ar{طريق} \ar{الخطأ}} — \emph{ʿan ṭarīq al-khaṭaʾ} — \textquotedblleft{}by mistake\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ar{أخذت} \ar{حقيبة} \ar{أخي} \ar{عن} \ar{طريق} \ar{الخطأ}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{akhadhtu ḥaqībat akhī ʿan ṭarīq al-khaṭaʾ.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
I took my brother’s bag by mistake.
\end{quote}

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ar{عن} \ar{طريق} \ar{الخطأ}} (\emph{ʿan ṭarīq al-khaṭaʾ}) is \textquotedblleft{}by way of the mistake\textquotedblright{}: \emph{khaṭaʾ} is built on the native Arabic root \emph{kh-ṭ-ʾ}, \textquotedblleft{}to miss the mark\textquotedblright{} (Lane), the root of the taught \emph{khaṭaʾ}.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling what happened.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright

  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{ʿan ṭarīq al-khaṭaʾ}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{akhadhtu ḥaqībat akhī ʿan ṭarīq al-khaṭaʾ.} — I took my brother’s bag by mistake.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Arabic for to inform the police, then the Arabic for for the first time, then say \emph{ʿan ṭarīq al-khaṭaʾ} again
\end{itemize}

\section[\texorpdfstring{\ar{أول} \ar{أمس} (awwal ams)}{أول أمس (awwal ams)}]{\ar{أول} \ar{أمس} (awwal ams) — the day before yesterday}

\label{lesson:AR-C349-awwal-ams}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Arabic for for the first time, then the Arabic for by mistake.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ar{أول} \ar{أمس}}
\textbf{\ar{أول} \ar{أمس}} — \emph{awwal ams} — \textquotedblleft{}the day before yesterday\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ar{وصل} \ar{خالي} \ar{أول} \ar{أمس}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{waṣala khālī awwal ams.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
My uncle arrived the day before yesterday.
\end{quote}

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ar{أول} \ar{أمس}} (\emph{awwal ams}) is \textquotedblleft{}the first of yesterday\textquotedblright{}: \emph{awwal}, first, is built on the native Arabic root \emph{ʾ-w-l} (Lane), before the taught \emph{ams}, yesterday.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling what happened.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{awwal ams}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{awwal ams}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{waṣala khālī awwal ams.} — My uncle arrived the day before yesterday.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Arabic for for the first time, then the Arabic for by mistake, then say \emph{awwal ams} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]

\section[\texorpdfstring{\ar{يوما} \ar{ما} (yawman mā)}{يوما ما (yawman mā)}]{\ar{يوما} \ar{ما} (yawman mā) — someday, one day}

\label{lesson:AR-C349-yawman-ma}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Arabic for by mistake, then the Arabic for the day before yesterday.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ar{يوما} \ar{ما}}
\textbf{\ar{يوما} \ar{ما}} — \emph{yawman mā} — \textquotedblleft{}someday, one day\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ar{سأزور} \ar{تلك} \ar{المدينة} \ar{يوما} \ar{ما}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{sa-azūru tilka al-madīna yawman mā.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
I will visit that city someday.
\end{quote}

Of the future; \ar{ذات} \ar{يوم} opens a story in the past.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ar{يوما} \ar{ما}} (\emph{yawman mā}) is \textquotedblleft{}on some day\textquotedblright{}: \emph{yawm} is usually traced to an inherited Semitic word for day, and \emph{mā} after it means \textquotedblleft{}some, any\textquotedblright{}.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling what happened.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{yawman mā}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{yawman mā}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{sa-azūru tilka al-madīna yawman mā.} — I will visit that city someday.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Arabic for by mistake, then the Arabic for the day before yesterday, then say \emph{yawman mā} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \ar{يوما} \ar{ما} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}Someday, one day\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[\texorpdfstring{\ar{عقب} (ʿaqiba)}{عقب (ʿaqiba)}]{\ar{عقب} (ʿaqiba) — right after, following}

\label{lesson:AR-C349-aqiba}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Arabic for the day before yesterday, then the Arabic for someday.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ar{عقب}}
\textbf{\ar{عقب}} — \emph{ʿaqiba} — \textquotedblleft{}right after, following\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ar{نام} \ar{الطفل} \ar{عقب} \ar{العشاء} \ar{مباشرة}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{nāma aṭ-ṭifl ʿaqiba al-ʿashāʾ mubāsharatan.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
The child fell asleep straight after dinner.
\end{quote}

A written word; \ar{بعد} is the everyday one.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ar{عقب}} (\emph{ʿaqiba}) is built on the native Arabic root \emph{ʿ-q-b} (Lane), the root of \emph{ʿaqib}, the heel. What comes \emph{ʿaqiba} a thing comes at its heels.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling what happened.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{ʿaqiba}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{ʿaqiba}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{nāma aṭ-ṭifl ʿaqiba al-ʿashāʾ mubāsharatan.} — The child fell asleep straight after dinner.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Arabic for the day before yesterday, then the Arabic for someday, then say \emph{ʿaqiba} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \ar{عقب} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}Right after, following\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
